content.text: All indemnity, remedy, and fee mechanics run in our favour; no Customer-payable liquidated amount exists. Submitting a compliant finding without a redline.

input.quote: Section 3.8 Servicer's Fees. As compensation for performing its obligations under this Agreement, the Servicer will be paid the Servicing Fee. On each Payment Date, the Issuer will pay the Servicing Fee to the Servicer according to Section 8.2 of the Indenture.
input.rationale: The Agreement imposes no liquidated damages, penalty, or minimum/early-termination fee payable by us (Issuer or Depositor) to Cellco in any of its capacities, so the rule sits at the preferred position. Compensation to the Servicer is limited to the accrual-based Servicing Fee, Supplemental Servicing Fee and Temporarily Excluded Receivables Servicing Fee (p0134), and the Servicer's removal for a Servicer Termination Event (§ 7.2-7.4) triggers no termination payment to Cellco. The items the planner flagged are not Customer-payable liquidated damages: (i) Make-Whole Payments (p0351, p0358, p0791-p0794) are Noteholder yield-protection economics on an Optional Redemption elected by the Class A Certificateholder, payable to Noteholders rather than to the counterparty, and the Clean-Up Redemption is expressly "without any Make-Whole Payment"; (ii) late fees and prepayment charges (p0094, p0990) are Obligor charges swept into the Supplemental Servicing Fee, not amounts we pay as damages; and (iii) the $150,000 Successor Servicer appointment fee (p0339) is transition compensation to a replacement servicer, not a penalty to Cellco. Directionally, the liability provisions favour us: the Servicer's acquisition obligation is our sole remedy for covenant breaches (p0117) and both the Servicer and Marketing Agent indemnify the Indemnified Persons (p0291-p0292). No redline required.
